fields.STRONGEST_PRO: Collectivism undermines individual rights by treating people as means to an end, denying their moral worth and stifling creativity, while prioritizing group interests over personal autonomy.
fields.STRONGEST_CON: Collectivism fosters social harmony, reduces conflict, and enables collective problem-solving, making societies more cohesive and effective through shared goals and mutual support.
fields.KEY_TENSION: PROs argue collectivism infringes on individual autonomy and rights; CONs claim it enhances social cohesion and collective efficacy through shared responsibility and cooperation.
fields.MISSING_PERSPECTIVES: The role of cultural context in valuing individualism vs. collectivism, potential benefits of hybrid systems balancing both, and how collectivism might address systemic inequalities without sacrificing individuality.
fields.OVERALL_BALANCE: Neutral, with compelling arguments on both sides: PROs emphasize individual rights and moral agency, while CONs highlight social unity and practical advantages of collective action.
